chief_complaint: progressive magnetic shuffling gait, urinary incontinence, and short-term memory loss over 1 year
hpi_details: 74M brought by daughter due to 1-year progressive triad of difficulty walking, urinary incontinence, and mild cognitive impairment. Daughter notes his feet seem 'glued to the floor' when initiating steps (magnetic gait), taking short shuffling steps. He has frequent bladder accidents without urge awareness and short-term memory forgetfulness.
ideas: daughter thinks he has Parkinson disease or rapid Alzheimer dementia
concerns: daughter worried he will fall and break his hip or require nursing home placement
expectations: wants specialized neurologist/neurosurgery evaluation to see if condition is reversible

clinical_knowledge.topic: Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus (NPH) evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus (NPH) is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management emphasizes Refer to neurosurgery for placement of a Ventriculoperitoneal (VP) shunt with programmable adjustable differential pressure valve to relieve ventriculomegaly and restore long-term gait and cognitive function, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: progressive magnetic shuffling gait, urinary incontinence, and short-term memory loss over 1 year

Key HPI features: 74M brought by daughter due to 1-year progressive triad of difficulty walking, urinary incontinence, and mild cognitive impairment. Daughter notes his feet seem 'glued to the floor' when initiating steps (magnetic gait), taking short shuffling steps. He has frequent bladder accidents without urge awareness and short-term memory forgetfulness.

Objective/Exam findings: Vitals: HR 68, BP 135/80. Neurological exam shows broad-based shuffling gait with start hesitation and impaired postural turning. No resting tremor, cogwheel rigidity, or bradykinesia of upper extremities. Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) 21/30 (deficits in attention and executive function). Non-contrast brain CT/MRI reveals ventriculomegaly disproportionate to cortical sulcal atrophy (Evans index > 0.3) with transependymal edema and crowding of high convexity sulci. High-volume lumbar puncture tap test (30 mL CSF removal) yields opening pressure of 14 cmH2O and produces dramatic improvement in gait speed and stride length within 2 hours.
Relevant background/PMH: Hypertension, Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia
Current medications: Amlodipine 5mg daily, Tamsulosin 0.4mg daily
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus (NPH).
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Parkinson's disease with dementia without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Repeated falls — significant injury risk while workup proceeds.
management_principles: Refer to neurosurgery for placement of a Ventriculoperitoneal (VP) shunt with programmable adjustable differential pressure valve to relieve ventriculomegaly and restore long-term gait and cognitive function
Assess clinical stability, monitor vital parameters, and perform targeted diagnostic investigations.
Implement targeted therapeutic interventions per evidence-based clinical practice guidelines.
Provide clear patient education, address patient concerns, and establish explicit follow-up and safety-netting instructions.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

learning_objectives: Recognize the classic Hakim-Adams clinical triad of Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus (wobbly, wet, and wacky: gait apraxia, urinary incontinence, dementia)
Differentiate NPH imaging features (ventriculomegaly with high convexity crowding, Evans index > 0.3) from ex-vacuo ventriculomegaly due to brain atrophy
Understand the diagnostic and prognostic utility of the high-volume lumbar puncture (CSF tap test)
Describe surgical management via Ventriculoperitoneal (VP) shunting and potential complications (overdrainage subdural hygroma)

teaching.one_liner: Enlarged brain ventricles causing the classic triad of a magnetic, shuffling gait, urinary incontinence, and cognitive decline — one of the few dementia-like conditions that can dramatically improve with a shunt.
red_flags: Repeated falls — significant injury risk while workup proceeds

must_ask.say: Does it look like his feet are stuck to the floor when he starts walking?
Has he had accidents without realizing his bladder was full?
How has his memory and thinking changed?
How many times has he fallen recently?
Which came first — the walking trouble or the memory problems?
